rationale: No displayed candidate plausibly supplied the child's detailed drafting template. C06 is the closest because it also invokes statutory authority to extend a prescribed compliance period for one year, but it concerns copyright formalities and lacks the child's distinctive customs machinery: separate extensions under sections 491, 557, and 559, serial further extensions during an emergency, bond-surety agreements, warehouse-proprietor consent, and preservation of prior actions under superseded proclamations. C23 shares customs terminology concerning entry or withdrawal from warehouse, while C12 concerns Treasury and customs authority, but neither parallels the child's operative structure. The child itself indicates that it supersedes an earlier 1943 proclamation amended in 1946; those undisplayed directives are much more likely sources of its template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: To extend the one-year period prescribed in section 491 ... for not more than one year
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the time within which compliance with such conditions and formalities may take place is hereby extended ... for one year
shared_material.explanation: C06 shares the concrete device of a presidentially authorized one-year statutory extension, but the surrounding legal predicates, beneficiaries, conditions, and administrative machinery are materially different.

shared_material.child_excerpt: merchandise ... entered for transportation in bond or for exportation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: articles ... entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption
shared_material.explanation: C23 uses related customs-entry and warehouse terminology, but only as part of an import restriction and does not reproduce the child's extension mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby authorize the Secretary of the Treasury
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of the Treasury is hereby designated and empowered
shared_material.explanation: C12 similarly delegates authority to the Treasury Secretary and addresses customs matters, but its catalog of delegated presidential functions does not parallel the child's emergency extensions or associated bond and warehouse conditions.
